title: LearnPyTorch · Autograd Lab
summary: See the chain rule, repair detached paths, inspect gradient accumulation, and debug a tiny training loop.
detail: 4 visual missions · Scalar autograd · Real PyTorch export
intro: Change the controls, predict the outcome, and inspect the actual backward contributions. Every graph node is selectable; playback can be paused or stepped manually.
scope: This browser lab implements first-order scalar reverse-mode differentiation for +, −, ×, ÷ and detach. It is not the full PyTorch runtime: no tensor autograd, GPU, higher-order derivatives, in-place operations or arbitrary Python execution. Training uses full-batch SGD on four points. Non-leaf values in the diagram are explanatory adjoints, not automatically retained .grad fields.
privacy: Progress is stored locally when available. Experiments run on your device. Python downloads reproduce your selected settings and require PyTorch to run.

ui.selectNode: Select a node to inspect the chain rule.
ui.gradientNote: The graph shows contributions within this backward pass. Parameter .grad buffers accumulate across passes; non-leaf .grad is not retained in ordinary PyTorch.
ui.cutNote: A dashed link carries the forward value but blocks the backward path.
ui.wrongPrediction: That prediction differs. Inspect the graph, then predict a fresh example.
ui.needTwo: Correct. Predict one more example to complete this mission.
ui.fixed: The repaired path produces the expected weight gradient on four examples.
ui.detachedError: The weight has no gradient. Reconnect its path to the loss.
ui.accumError: After two passes, the stored gradient should equal this pass’s gradient. Clear it before each independent backward.
ui.trainFail: The loss did not fall enough on both datasets. Inspect the operation order and learning rate.
ui.trainPass: The repaired loop reduces mean squared error on both datasets.
ui.storage: Storage is unavailable; progress lasts for this visit.
ui.numericError: The calculation exceeded this lab’s numerical limits. Reset or lower the learning rate.
ui.graphError: The loop tried to use a missing or already-consumed graph. Build a fresh forward graph before each backward.
ui.chartNote: The loss chart uses log(1 + loss) to keep divergent and convergent runs visible. The table shows exact numeric values.
ui.noGradient: This value has no path that requires gradients.

missions.title: Follow the chain rule
missions.intro: A scalar prediction is enough to reveal how gradients travel. The same error is used twice when computing error × error.
missions.goal: Predict w.grad correctly on two different examples, then trace each backward contribution.
missions.concept: Each edge multiplies an incoming gradient by a local derivative. When a value is used twice, both contributions must be added.
missions.hint: For loss = (w*x+b-target)², w.grad = 2*(w*x+b-target)*x. Watch the two edges leaving loss.
missions.transfer: What changes when x is negative? Why can a parameter receive zero gradient even when the loss is positive?

missions.title: Find the broken path
missions.intro: The prediction can look correct while one parameter cannot learn. A detached value still participates in the forward calculation.
missions.goal: Reconnect w to the loss so its gradient is computed correctly on four examples.
missions.concept: detach() preserves the numerical value but stops gradient tracking through that branch. Here b still receives a gradient, so backward itself can succeed.
missions.hint: Turn off “Detach w before multiplying”, run backward, and inspect w. The prediction value stays the same.
missions.transfer: When would intentionally detaching a target or teacher output be useful? Which model should receive gradients?

missions.title: Separate a derivative from a buffer
missions.intro: Two identical backward passes can produce the same derivatives and a different stored parameter gradient.
missions.goal: Run two fresh forward/backward passes while keeping w.grad equal to the derivative from one pass.
missions.concept: Backward adds to leaf .grad buffers. Clear them between independent optimization steps. Deliberate microbatch accumulation is useful, but requires appropriate loss scaling.
missions.hint: Enable clearing before each backward, then run two passes. Compare the graph contribution with the stored w.grad.
missions.transfer: For two unequal microbatches, how would you scale their mean losses to match the full-batch mean gradient?

missions.title: Make the model learn
missions.intro: Fit y = 2x + 1 using four points and two scalar parameters. The starter loop updates before it has computed any gradients.
missions.goal: Reorder the four operations so 12 steps bring mean squared error below 2% of its initial value on both the visible dataset and a second dataset.
missions.concept: A typical step clears old gradients, computes a fresh loss, calls backward, then updates parameters. optimizer.step() does not calculate gradients or clear them.
missions.hint: Use clear → forward → backward → update. Start with learning rate 0.1, then compare a much larger rate.
missions.transfer: Why does clearing gradients immediately after backward prevent learning? Export the repaired loop and check it in real PyTorch.
